analysis.title: Global Healthcare: Pharmaceuticals: Key takeaways from our lung cancer KOL event at ESMO
key_insights: A lung cancer KOL called AMGN's DeLLphi-305 (Imdelltra + Imfinzi maintenance in extensive-stage small cell lung cancer) the single most practice-changing readout at ESMO. Median OS was 21.1 vs 12.7 months (HR=0.42, p<0.001) and median PFS was 7.4 vs 1.9 months (HR=0.34, p<0.001) versus Imfinzi alone.
The KOL expects Imdelltra + Imfinzi to become the standard maintenance regimen after regulatory approval.

About 10-20% of ES-SCLC patients progress rapidly or decline functionally during induction and never reach maintenance. This supports moving T-cell engagers into frontline induction, but Phase 3 induction combination trials will take time to mature.

With Imdelltra as the maintenance backbone, the KOL expects emerging DLL3-directed ADCs to be positioned mainly in second line, after progression on DLL3xCD3 bispecific maintenance, rather than competing in frontline.

MRK/Kelun's sac-TMT + Keytruda in frontline PD-L1-negative (TPS <1%) non-squamous NSCLC (OptiTROP-Lung06) had median PFS of 15.0 vs 5.7 months (HR=0.49, p<0.0001) against Keytruda + chemotherapy. Interim OS favored sac-TMT (HR=0.58).
If statistically significant OS is confirmed in global studies such as the TroFuse program, replacing platinum-pemetrexed with sac-TMT could change standard practice in PD-L1-negative NSCLC.

Grade 3+ hematologic toxicity was lower with sac-TMT than chemotherapy (severe anemia 6.1% vs 20.4%). ADC-specific oral stomatitis is more persistent, lasting months rather than weeks. Chinese trial populations are younger and often capped at age <75, which can flatter tolerability versus Western trials.

The KOL sees no meaningful efficacy difference between BNTX/BMY's pumitamig (PD-L1xVEGF) and SMMT/Akeso's ivonescimab (PD-1xVEGF), and half-lives are comparable. BNTX has a stronger base of non-Chinese global trial data, so long-term differentiation may depend on how fast global Phase 3 programs are deployed across tumor types.

Pumitamig combined with DualityBio's B7-H3 ADC elfe-D showed promising early efficacy with manageable tolerability and minimal overlapping toxicity. The KOL sees ADCs as a rational pairing with PD-(L)1xVEGF bispecifics, with the bispecific potentially driving an OS tail effect.

The KOL believes SMMT's global Phase 3 HARMONi-3 squamous NSCLC cohort is likely to read out positive, based on consistent PD-(L)1xVEGF efficacy in squamous histology and Akeso's China-only HARMONi-6.

On HARMONi-3, a PFS HR below 0.65 would confidently suggest a statistically significant OS benefit. The KOL said a PFS HR above 0.65 could also translate to significant OS, given Akeso's updated HARMONi-6 PFS data.

The KOL assigns a ~70-75% probability of success to MRNA/MRK's intismeran in the ongoing Phase 3 in resectable NSCLC. The reasoning is that the mRNA platform may produce a more persistent neoantigen-specific T-cell response than failed peptide vaccines, and that adjuvant Keytruda adds only modest benefit after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy.
In renal cell carcinoma, which has a lower tumor mutational burden than melanoma or NSCLC, the KOL is cautiously optimistic on intismeran. A negative RCC result would not read through to NSCLC.

The KOL is cautious on AZN/Daiichi's Phase 3 AVANZAR (Dato-DXd + Imfinzi + chemotherapy vs Keytruda + chemotherapy, frontline NSCLC), assigning 50/50 odds of success in the TROP2-QCS biomarker-positive subgroup because the biomarker was identified retrospectively. The KOL sees no read-through from the readout delays, and a statistically significant OS HR ≤0.75 would drive clinical adoption.

The KOL called Roche's divarasib Krascendo 1 data (KRAS G12C) practice-changing alongside DeLLphi-305. It showed an OS benefit in KRAS G12C-mutated NSCLC and supports future standard-of-care status upon approval.

The KOL is skeptical that TIL therapy is feasible in lung cancer. Tumor harvesting and ex-vivo expansion are operationally complex, and the IL-2 requirement may add substantial toxicity, so TIL will likely be a niche product.

market_movers.rationale: DeLLphi-305 data viewed by the KOL as the most practice-changing ESMO readout, establishing Imdelltra + Imfinzi as the expected post-induction maintenance standard. PT of $481 is DCF-based (2.5% TGR, 8% WACC).
Sac-TMT OptiTROP-Lung06 (with Kelun) and intismeran (with MRNA) both read favorably in the KOL discussion. PT based on 16x P/E on Q5-Q8 adjusted EPS.

KOL sees a high probability of success for global Phase 3 HARMONi-3 squamous NSCLC cohort, supported by Akeso's HARMONi-6. PT blends an 85%/15% risk-adjusted DCF value of $37 and a theoretical M&A value of $77.

Pumitamig data encouraging, with a stronger base of global trial data than ivonescimab. KOL sees no efficacy differentiation, so positioning may hinge on global Phase 3 deployment speed. PT is DCF-based (11% WACC, 1% TGR).
Pumitamig partner with BNTX. PT based on 10.0x Q5-Q8 EPS.
KOL assigns ~70-75% PoS to intismeran in adjuvant/resectable NSCLC and is cautiously optimistic in RCC. PT is 100% DCF (11% WACC, 5% TGR).
Kelun Biotech (6990.HK, no US listing) is the developer of sac-TMT, whose OptiTROP-Lung06 data impressed the KOL. TP is risk-adjusted DCF (11% discount rate, 3% terminal growth).

sector_views.rationale: The note is a KOL event summary and does not state a sector stance. It covers practice-changing data in SCLC maintenance, KRAS G12C NSCLC and TROP2 ADCs, and a crowded PD-(L)1xVEGF field.

risk_factors: SMMT: data from Akeso in China may not translate to global studies, plus U.S.-China trade, safety or delay risk, competitor PD-1/L1xVEGF assets with better data, and financing/dilution.
AMGN: biosimilar and generic erosion, crowded competition, pipeline failure, reimbursement, IP, regulatory risk, and tax litigation with the IRS (company estimate of $8.7bn for 2010-2015 alone).
MRK: faster Keytruda loss-of-exclusivity erosion or weaker conversion to SubQ Keytruda, vaccine slowdown, pipeline disappointments, and FDA/tariff/regulatory risk.
BNTX: BNT327 clinical failure and risk that its profile is considered materially inferior to SMMT's ivonescimab.
MRNA: failure to show proof of concept in additional modalities or indications, IP, manufacturing, financing/dilution, and payor pushback.

BMY: faster erosion of the legacy portfolio from loss of exclusivity and IRA, slower growth-portfolio ramp, and negative pipeline outcomes such as Cobenfy in Alzheimer's disease psychosis and milvexian.
Kelun: R&D risk in new indications, heated ADC competition, limited commercial track record, talent competition, and partnership risk.
AVANZAR carries 50/50 odds of success in the biomarker-positive subgroup, and the QCS biomarker was identified retrospectively.
geopolitical: U.S.-China trade relations are cited as a risk to SMMT's supply chain operations.
Data generated by Akeso in China may not translate to SMMT's global studies. Chinese trial populations are younger and subject to age caps.

tension_points.bull_case: Pumitamig (BNTX/BMY) and ivonescimab (SMMT/Akeso) show consistent efficacy and comparable half-lives. The KOL sees a high probability of success for HARMONi-3 squamous NSCLC and promising pumitamig + B7-H3 ADC combinations.
tension_points.bear_case: The KOL sees no efficacy differentiation between the two bispecifics, so winners may be set by how fast global Phase 3 programs deploy. GS's own BNTX risk list flags BNT327 being viewed as materially inferior to ivonescimab, and SMMT's risks include China data not translating globally.
tension_points.what_invalidates: For HARMONi-3, a PFS HR above 0.65 is a weaker signal, though the KOL says it could still translate to statistically significant OS.

tension_points.bull_case: Sac-TMT + Keytruda cut risk of progression or death by about half in PD-L1-negative non-squamous NSCLC (PFS HR=0.49), with lower severe anemia than chemotherapy.
tension_points.bear_case: ADC stomatitis is more persistent. Chinese trial populations are younger and age-capped, which may flatter tolerability. AVANZAR (AZN/Daiichi) is rated only 50/50 in the biomarker-positive subgroup.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Failure of global studies to confirm a statistically significant OS benefit would weaken the case for replacing chemotherapy. For AVANZAR, a statistically significant OS HR ≤0.75 would support adoption.
